topic: How do GEO versus LEO satellite orbits impact power flux density and resolution trade-offs in passive radar systems using Inmarsat and Iridium?
consensus_response: The comparison of power flux densities between Inmarsat and Iridium reveals that, despite their vastly different orbital heights, both systems offer similar power flux densities at the Earth's surface (64-70 dBm/m²). However, Inmarsat's higher orbit leads to lower flux density due to increased path loss, impacting the system's ability to achieve high resolution. Inmarsat's higher SNR and signal-to-clutter ratios are advantageous, but Iridium's greater number of satellites provides more opportunities to avoid unfavorable geometries, enhancing flexibility. A trade-off between power flux density and resolution is observed, where higher power flux density achieved by Inmarsat comes at the cost of reduced resolution due to increased path loss.
